input_messages.content: Hi there! I’m having trouble with my mobile data—it either stops working or is extremely slow. I really need to get excellent internet speed on my phone, especially since I don’t have access to Wi-Fi right now. Can you help me fix this?
Sure! My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.
It looks like my phone is currently in Airplane Mode. Should I turn off Airplane Mode to continue with the troubleshooting?
I've turned off Airplane Mode. Now, my status bar shows a poor signal, 2G network, and data is enabled. The internet still seems very slow. What should I do next?
My phone is currently set to "2G only" for the network mode. Could you guide me on how to change it to "4G/5G preferred"? I’m not sure where to find that setting.

I've changed the network mode to "4G/5G preferred." Now my status bar shows an excellent signal and 5G is active, with data enabled. What would you like me to do next? Should I test my internet speed now?

I tried running a speed test, but it failed and said "No Connection." Even though my status bar shows 5G with an excellent signal, it seems like the internet still isn't working. What should I do next?
I checked my SIM card status, and it shows as active and working. What should I check next?
I checked my APN settings. The APN name is set to "internet" and the MMSC URL is "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." Nothing looks empty or obviously incorrect to me. What should I do next?
I reset my APN settings to default and rebooted my phone, but when I tried the speed test again, it still failed and said "No Connection." What should I try next?
Let’s try a few more advanced troubleshooting steps first. I’d really like to get this working with excellent internet speed if possible. What should I do next?

I checked everything you mentioned: Data Saver mode is off, there’s no VPN active, and I toggled mobile data off and back on. Unfortunately, when I tried the speed test again, it still failed with "No Connection." Is there anything else I can try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated since I really need excellent internet speed for my work.

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hi there! I’m having trouble with my mobile data—it either stops working or is extremely slow. I really need to get excellent internet speed on my phone, especially since I don’t have access to Wi-Fi right now. Can you help me fix this?

I can help you troubleshoot your mobile data issues. First, I need to identify your account to check your line and plan details. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID?

Once I have this information, I’ll guide you through the steps to resolve your mobile data problem.
Sure! My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.

Thank you for providing your information, John. To help you fix your mobile data issue, I’ll need you to perform a few quick checks on your phone. This will help us identify the cause of the slow or non-working data.

Are you able to check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- If you see any icons like “✈️ Airplane Mode,” “📵 No Signal,” or “📱 Data Enabled/Disabled”?
- What network type is displayed (e.g., 5G, 4G, LTE, 3G, etc.)?
- Your current signal strength (bars or description)?

If you’re not sure how to check, let me know and I can guide you through the steps!
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
It looks like my phone is currently in Airplane Mode. Should I turn off Airplane Mode to continue with the troubleshooting?

Yes, please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. Airplane Mode disables all wireless connections, including mobile data, which is likely the reason your data isn’t working.

Once you’ve turned off Airplane Mode, check if your mobile data starts working or if you see a network signal (like 4G, 5G, or LTE) in your status bar. Let me know what you see after turning it off, and if your data connection improves. If not, we’ll continue troubleshooting!

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I've turned off Airplane Mode. Now, my status bar shows a poor signal, 2G network, and data is enabled. The internet still seems very slow. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Since your phone is connected to a 2G network with a poor signal, this is likely the main reason for your slow internet speed. To improve your data speed, you should switch your network mode preference to allow 4G or 5G, which provide much faster data.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to change your network mode to “4G/5G preferred” on your phone? If so, please let me know your phone’s make and model (e.g., iPhone 13, Samsung Galaxy S21), or I can provide general instructions if you prefer.
Network Mode Preference: 2g_only
My phone is currently set to "2G only" for the network mode. Could you guide me on how to change it to "4G/5G preferred"? I’m not sure where to find that setting.

Certainly! Here are general steps to change your network mode to “4G/5G preferred” on most Android phones:

1. Open the **Settings** app on your phone.
2. Tap on **Connections** or **Network & Internet** (the exact name may vary).
3. Select **Mobile Network** or **Cellular Networks**.
4. Tap on **Preferred network type** or **Network mode**.
5. Choose **4G/5G preferred** (sometimes listed as “LTE/5G/4G/3G/2G (auto connect)”).

If you’re using an iPhone:
1. Open the **Settings** app.
2. Tap **Cellular**.
3. Tap **Cellular Data Options**.
4. Tap **Voice & Data**.
5. Select **5G Auto** or **4G**.

After making this change, wait a few moments for your phone to reconnect. Check your status bar to see if it now shows 4G or 5G, and test your internet speed again.

Let me know if you need more specific instructions for your phone model, or if you run into any issues during this process!

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I've changed the network mode to "4G/5G preferred." Now my status bar shows an excellent signal and 5G is active, with data enabled. What would you like me to do next? Should I test my internet speed now?

Yes, please go ahead and test your internet speed now. This will help us confirm if your data connection is performing at an excellent level with the new network mode.

Let me know the results of your speed test, including whether your browsing and app usage feel much faster. If you still experience issues, we can continue troubleshooting further.
Speed test failed: No Connection.

I tried running a speed test, but it failed and said "No Connection." Even though my status bar shows 5G with an excellent signal, it seems like the internet still isn't working. What should I do next?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your phone shows a strong 5G signal but you still have no internet connection, the issue may be related to your SIM card or your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings.

Let’s start by checking your SIM card status. Please check your SIM card status in your phone’s settings and let me know if it shows as “Active,” “Missing,” or “Locked.” If you need instructions on how to check this, let me know your phone model, or I can provide general steps.
Your SIM card is active and working.
I checked my SIM card status, and it shows as active and working. What should I check next?

Great, your SIM card is active. The next step is to check your APN (Access Point Name) settings, as incorrect APN settings can prevent your phone from accessing mobile data even with a strong signal.

Please check your APN settings and let me know if anything looks incorrect or if the APN/MMSC fields are empty. If you’re unsure how to check this, let me know your phone model, or I can provide general instructions.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
I checked my APN settings. The APN name is set to "internet" and the MMSC URL is "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." Nothing looks empty or obviously incorrect to me. What should I do next?

Thank you for checking your APN settings. Since your SIM is active and your APN settings appear correct, but you still have no data connection, the next step is to reset your APN settings to default. Sometimes, even if the settings look correct, a reset can resolve hidden configuration issues.

Please reset your APN settings to default on your phone. After resetting, you must reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings and reboot your phone, or are you comfortable doing this on your own? Let me know if you need guidance!

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I reset my APN settings to default and rebooted my phone, but when I tried the speed test again, it still failed and said "No Connection." What should I try next?

Thank you for following those steps. Since you still have no data connection after resetting your APN settings and rebooting, let’s check if your line has reached its monthly data limit, which could cause a loss of connectivity.

I will now check your current data usage and plan details to see if you’ve exceeded your data allowance.
